executive_decision.rationale: The project has a world-class governance and validation infrastructure (Governance 95/100, Infrastructure 85/100) sitting atop a Part 1 content pool that is structurally immature (45/100). The infrastructure can validate and protect — but it cannot create. The content authoring pipeline that produced all 2,540 items is the root cause of 8 defect classes. Expanding to Part 2 through the same pipeline would inject the same DL-008/DL-013/DL-026/DL-031 defects into a fresh content pool, requiring the same years-long remediation program that Part 1 is still undergoing.

alternative_assessed.reason: Even 'targeted' expansion (e.g., 50-100 Part 2 items as a pilot) requires the quality-first authoring pipeline, which has zero validated items. Targeted expansion through the existing template-rotation pipeline would produce defect-bearing items that require remediation before they can enter the learner pool — defeating the purpose of a pilot. The pipeline must be validated on Part 1 items first, where the content domain expertise already exists.

methodology_notes.weighting_rationale: Content Maturity (30%) and Governance (25%) are weighted highest because they directly determine whether Part 2 items would be (a) accurate and (b) protected. Infrastructure (20%) is next because it's the execution layer. Pipeline (15%) and Organizational (10%) are trailing indicators of sustained delivery capability.
methodology_notes.scoring_method: Each dimension score is a weighted composite of sub-components. Weights sum to 100. Overall score = Σ(weight × score/100).
methodology_notes.thresholds: ≥80 = READY, 65-79 = PARTIALLY READY, <65 = NOT READY. Two dimensions scoring <65 constitutes a BLOCK regardless of overall score.
methodology_notes.variance_from_template: The executive template showed 58/100 overall. Corrected to 65/100 via verified arithmetic: 13.5 + 23.75 + 17.0 + 3.75 + 7.2 = 65.2 → 65. The 58 appears to have been a pre-verification estimate.
